high.title: US-Iran Tensions Escalate in Strait of Hormuz, Tanker Ships Turning Back
high.summary: Iran has repeatedly attacked tankers in the Strait of Hormuz since July 6, with at least nine ships attacked according to IMO data, causing a significant decline in vessel traffic through this critical oil shipping lane. One seafarer was killed and multiple others injured in separate attacks on oil tankers. This escalation poses a direct threat to global oil supply chains and could drive up energy prices, significantly impacting Indonesia's fuel import costs and Pertamina's operations.

high.title: Indonesia Becomes Founding Member of World AI Cooperation Organization (WAICO) with China
high.summary: Indonesia officially became one of the founding nations of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO), signed in Shanghai under direction from President Prabowo Subianto. As a founding member, Indonesia gains first-access rights to all AI development discussions within the organization. This marks a significant strategic move for Indonesia's digital economy positioning and international technology governance influence.

high.title: Indonesia Signs WAICO Declaration, Ready to Strengthen Global AI Cooperation
high.summary: Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto signed the Agreement on the Establishment of WAICO in Shanghai, acting on President Prabowo's directive from a cabinet meeting on July 13. WAICO is established as an independent intergovernmental international organization with international legal personality. This positions Indonesia at the forefront of global AI governance, with potential long-term implications for digital investment flows and tech policy frameworks.

high.title: US-Iran Tensions Escalate in Strait of Hormuz, Tankers Turn Back
high.summary: Iran has attacked at least nine vessels since July 6 in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a significant decline in shipping traffic through this critical oil chokepoint. One sailor was killed and multiple others injured in separate tanker attacks near Oman. This escalation poses a direct threat to global oil supply chains and could drive up energy prices, with significant implications for Indonesia's fuel imports and energy costs.

high.title: IHSG Ends Week on a High Note, Rises to 6,175 as Foreign Investors Net Buy Rp 638 Billion
high.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) surged 4.24% over the trading week of July 13-17, 2026, closing at 6,175.535 — recovering from 5,924.360 the previous Friday. Foreign investors recorded a net buy of Rp 638.05 billion on Friday alone, signaling renewed short-term interest in Indonesian equities. However, cumulative net foreign selling for 2026 remains deeply negative at over Rp 75.71 trillion, highlighting persistent structural outflow concerns.

high.title: IHSG Closes Thursday in the Green, Up 1.10% to 6,108 Amid Foreign Inflows and Banking Sector Gains
high.summary: The IHSG rose 1.10% on Thursday, July 16, 2026, to 6,108.21, supported by gains in major stocks ASII, BMRI, and BBCA, while all sectors closed in positive territory with technology leading at +1.94%. Foreign investors posted a net buy of Rp 283.41 billion on the regular market and approximately Rp 1.22 trillion across all markets, partly driven by a negotiated block transaction in PKPK shares worth over Rp 1 trillion. Meanwhile, U.S. markets weakened, with the Nasdaq falling 1.47%, though MSCI Indonesia and ETF EIDO both posted gains.

medium.title: Tax Directorate General Introduces New Methods to Enforce Taxpayer Compliance
medium.summary: Indonesia's Directorate General of Taxation (DJP) has issued Circular Letter SE-8/PJ/2026, introducing two new data collection methods — field visits to taxpayer locations and non-field technology-based surveillance — to boost tax compliance. This regulatory change signals a more aggressive enforcement posture by tax authorities, which Indonesian businesses and individuals should be aware of. Companies operating in Indonesia may face increased scrutiny of their tax obligations.

medium.title: National Nutrition Agency (BGN) Carries IDR 1.6 Trillion in Unpaid Debt from 2025
medium.summary: Indonesia's National Nutrition Agency (BGN) has disclosed IDR 1.6 trillion in outstanding payables to third-party vendors for services already completed in the 2025 fiscal year that have yet to be paid. The agency plans to settle these arrears through the 2026 budget allocation (DIPA 2026). This raises concerns about fiscal management and cash flow risks for vendors and contractors involved in government nutrition programs.

medium.title: Pertamina Reports Fuel Supply Situation in North Sumatra Returning to Normal
medium.summary: Pertamina Patra Niaga reports that fuel distribution in North Sumatra is normalizing following a recent supply disruption, with queues at gas stations gradually clearing. Independent Commissioner Prabu Revolusi confirmed improvement through CCTV monitoring and direct field inspections, urging the public not to panic or over-purchase. The resolution of the supply disruption is a positive signal for regional energy stability, though it highlights ongoing vulnerabilities in Pertamina's distribution network.

medium.title: Indonesia Eyes Huawei and ByteDance Partnerships as Co-Founder of Global AI Organization
medium.summary: Coordinating Minister Airlangga Hartarto met with top executives from Huawei and ByteDance in Shanghai to explore cooperation in AI, digital infrastructure, digital talent development, and technology investment. Huawei brings strengths in telecom infrastructure, cloud computing, and AI, while ByteDance offers expertise through platforms such as TikTok, CapCut, and Lark. These discussions signal potential large-scale Chinese technology investment into Indonesia's digital sector.

medium.title: Indonesian Coffee Breaks Into Morocco and China Markets via Warehouse Receipt System
medium.summary: Indonesia's Commodity Futures Trading Supervisory Agency (Bappebti) exported two containers of coffee totaling 38.4 tons worth approximately USD 227,443 to China and Morocco, dispatched from the KAI-ASLI Warehouse Receipt System facility in Bandung. An additional eight containers of Arabica Semi-Wash coffee (153.6 tons, ~USD 1.25 million) are set to follow to China. This demonstrates the effectiveness of Indonesia's Warehouse Receipt System in boosting commodity export competitiveness and expanding global market access for local farmers.

medium.title: Government Launches New Methods to Track Tax Compliance, Including Tech Surveillance and Field Visits
medium.summary: Indonesia's Directorate General of Taxes (DJP) has issued Circular Letter SE-8/PJ/2026, introducing two new methods to monitor taxpayer compliance: direct field visits to residences and business locations, and non-field data collection using information technology. This represents a significant tightening of tax enforcement that businesses and individual taxpayers across Indonesia should be aware of. The move signals the government's intensified effort to broaden the tax base and improve revenue collection.

medium.title: National Nutrition Agency (BGN) Carries Rp 1.6 Trillion in Unpaid Debts from 2025
medium.summary: Indonesia's National Nutrition Agency (BGN) has disclosed Rp 1.6 trillion in outstanding payables to third-party vendors from fiscal year 2025 for completed activities that have not yet been paid. The agency plans to settle these obligations through the 2026 budget allocation (DIPA 2026). This raises concerns about fiscal management and payment reliability for vendors and contractors working with government nutrition programs.

medium.title: Pertamina Reports Fuel Supply in North Sumatra Returning to Normal After Disruption
medium.summary: Pertamina Patra Niaga reports that fuel distribution in North Sumatra is normalizing following a recent supply disruption, with queues at gas stations easing based on CCTV monitoring and field inspections. The company's independent commissioner assured that fuel stocks in the region are adequate and urged residents not to panic-buy. This update is relevant for monitoring Pertamina's operational stability and regional energy security.

medium.title: Four Companies in IPO Pipeline at Indonesia Stock Exchange — Here's What We Know
medium.summary: As of July 17, 2026, four companies are queued for IPO listing on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX), comprising two small-asset firms (below Rp 50 billion) and two large-asset firms (above Rp 250 billion). The prospective issuers span three sectors: basic materials, consumer non-cyclicals, and healthcare (two companies). This signals continued, albeit modest, activity in Indonesia's primary equity market.
